text:
priya.patel: Hey team — customer (private VPC, Azure) hitting failures during our onprem installer and runtime pulls. Symptoms: model shard pulls time out, auth requests to token endpoint fail with TLS handshake errors. Example from agent log: `2024-05-12T17:12:03Z error transport: tls: handshake failure` and `GET https://registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net/v1/models/12345 -> 403`. They also see `curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca`

oncall-sre: Thanks — can you get me the minimal repro steps and a quick `dig` / `curl` from the VM that runs the installer? Need to confirm DNS and TLS. Example commands to run:```bash
# DNS
dig +short registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net
# tls check
curl -v --resolve registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net:443:52.12.34.56 https://registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net/v1/health
# check OCSP
openssl s_client -connect registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net:443 -status < /dev/null
```

priya.patel: Got a curl output from customer, pasted below (redacted IP):```* Rebuilt URL to: https://registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net/v1/health
*   Trying 52.12.34.56...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net (52.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* Server certificate: proxy-corp-intercept.local
* SSL: certificate subject name (proxy-corp-intercept.local) does not match registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net
* More details: alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (proxy-corp-intercept.local) does not match registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net
```They confirmed their infra team runs TLS intercepting proxy for egress.

alex.chen: This looks like TLS MITM / corporate proxy causing SNI mismatch and unknown CA. For our onprem flow customers usually need these egress rules (hostname + port + optional IP ranges) — ask infra to allow passthrough or install the proxy CA into the runtime's trust store. Minimal allowlist we recommend (hostname-based, port 443):
- registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net
- shards.redwoodmodels.com
- model-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com
- telemetry.collect.redwood.com
- auth.token.redwood.com
- oauth2.redwood.com
- files.redwood.dev
- kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com (or region-specific KMS endpoints)
- crl.ocsp.redwood.com (OCSP/CRL checks)

If they cannot do hostname passthrough, they must allow these IP ranges for NAT egress. Short example ip blocks we use across providers (confirm for customer's region):
- 52.12.0.0/16 (example AWS range)
- 34.200.0.0/14
- 18.196.0.0/15
(we'll ask infra for exact ranges after region confirmation).

Also: if their proxy terminates TLS they need to allow `OCSP` and `CRL` endpoints used by our certs and ensure the corporate CA is trusted by the agent process. Suggest steps to verify trust:```bash
# check cert chain via openssl
openssl s_client -showcerts -servername registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net -connect registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net:443
# test real backend without proxy by hitting known ip (if allowed)
curl -v --connect-to registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net:443:52.12.34.56 https://registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net/v1/health
```

oncall-sre: Also call out telemetry and auth endpoints — if telemetry is blocked our telemetry pings will fail (non-blocking but noisy). For auth: failing to reach `auth.token.redwood.com` will cause token fetch errors and cascade to 403s for model pulls. If they want a minimal allowlist to unblock installs and runtime, allow: `auth.token.redwood.com`, `registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net`, `shards.redwoodmodels.com`, and S3 endpoints used for artifacts.

casey: Adding order-of-operations for customer's infra team: 1) verify corporate proxy is not rewriting SNI; 2) if it is, either enable TLS passthrough for the above hosts or import corporate CA into agent/container trust store; 3) whitelist OCSP endpoints and AWS/Cloud provider IP ranges for model artifact fetch; 4) confirm `curl -v` shows the server cert subject as our host (not `proxy-corp-*`).

priya.patel: Thanks — passing this to the customer with the exact host list and the openssl/curl commands. Also asking region and cloud provider to provide exact IP ranges. They'll try enabling passthrough first. I'll update thread once they test. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Automated note: created support ticket #SUP-2024-4527 and linked to KB article `onprem-egress-checklist-v2`.

priya.patel: One more thing — customer asked if we can provide a smaller, strictly minimal host subset for a locked-down environment. Alex, can you supply a "bootstrap" list (installer + auth) we can give to security teams?

alex.chen: Yup — bootstrap (installer only): `files.redwood.dev`, `auth.token.redwood.com`, `registry-proxy.redwood-infra.net`, `model-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com`. Note that full runtime needs shards + telemetry to operate normally.

priya.patel: Perfect — sending now. Will follow up after they test passthrough.
